commander_identity.mechanical_plan: Don Andres, the Renegade ({1}{U}{B}{R} 4/3 legendary Vampire Pirate): (1) creatures we control but don't own get +2/+2, menace, deathtouch and are Pirates in addition to their other types (613.1b type, 613.4c P/T layer); (2) whenever we cast a noncreature spell we don't own, create two tapped Treasures (111.10a). Ownership (108.3, 110.2, 111.2): a copy we create is ours and is not cast (707.10), so only real opposing cards count. Theft: Treachery (new), Hostage Taker, Gilded Drake, Insurrection, Coercive Recruiter, Thieving Amalgam manifests (opponent-owned face-down 2/2s, 701.40a, which Don makes 4/4 menace deathtouch Pirates), Jhoira, Praetor's Grasp/Black Cat/Outrageous Robbery exiles, Animate Dead/Reanimate on opposing graveyards, Hurl Through Hell. Foreign casts (Don Treasures): Gríma and Fallen Shinobi (new), Etali, Plargg and Nassari, Grenzo, Ramirez, Laughing Jasper Flint, Locke, Stolen Strategy, Wand of Wonder, Siphon Insight, Arcane Heist, You Find Some Prisoners, Thief of Sanity, Gonti, Ragavan, Dauthi Voidwalker, Opposition Agent, Tasha, Brainstealer Dragon, Decadent Dragon. Pirate payoffs: Admiral Beckett Brass, Malcolm, both Breeches, Coercive Recruiter, Kindred Discovery, Roaming Throne, Vaan.
commander_identity.natural_ceiling: Power Bracket 4 (Optimized). Game Changers: 5 in baseline and candidate (Ancient Tomb, Cyclonic Rift, Fierce Guardianship, Opposition Agent, Vampiric Tutor). Commander Spellbook find-my-combos: 0 included combos for both lists (almost-included 23 -> 19). No infinite is claimed.
commander_identity.anti_homogenization: Commander-first: every add serves Don's own Oracle, either casting opponent-owned cards (Gríma, Fallen Shinobi), stealing permanently so Don's static applies (Treachery), or getting Don onto the battlefield untapped-on-curve (two Verges). Owner-removed classes (the 2026-10-14 removals: Buried Alive/Living Death/Victimize reanimation, Cunning Rhetoric, Share the Spoils, The Ruinous Powers, Revel in Riches, Gonti, Lord of Luxury, Zara, four slow/tapped lands; and the same-day rejections Mind's Dilation, Xanathar, Agent of Treachery, Bribery, Captivating Crew, Memory Plunder) were judged and not re-added. Distinctness (nonbasic names shared, baseline -> candidate): Nathan Drake, Treasure Hunter 62 -> 61; Admiral Brass, Unsinkable 55 -> 53; Admiral Beckett Brass 54 -> 52; Edward Kenway 49 -> 49; Cormela, Glamour Thief 31 -> 31; Evelyn, the Covetous 27 -> 28 (Blazemire Verge is in Evelyn). Disclosed honestly: Gríma is in the Nathan Drake list, and the cuts Professional Face-Breaker and Blasphemous Act are also in Nathan Drake; Shipwreck Marsh and Smoldering Marsh are in Admiral Brass, Unsinkable. The candidate reduces overlap with the pirate decks by 0-2 names only; separation is commander-first: Don rewards control-without-ownership (+2/+2, menace, deathtouch, Pirate) and casting opponent-owned noncreature spells (two tapped Treasures), so the adds cast opponent cards (Gríma, Shinobi) or steal permanently (Treachery), not generic Pirate tribal or our own impulse draw.

whole_deck_audit.roles_and_overlaps:
All 99 library cards were reviewed by quantity (98 rows: 2x Island, everything else 1x; Mountain and Swamp one each).
Roles:
- 35 lands: Ancient Tomb, Cavern of Souls (Pirate), Path of Ancestry, Command Tower, City of Brass, Mana Confluence, Exotic Orchard, Otawara, Takenuma, Training Center, Luxury Suite, Morphic Pool, Xander's Lounge, six fetches, three originals (Badlands, Underground Sea, Volcanic Island), three shocks (Blood Crypt, Steam Vents, Watery Grave), Sulfur Falls, three pain lands (Shivan Reef, Sulfurous Springs, Underground River), Shipwreck Marsh and Smoldering Marsh (cut; Gloomlake and Blazemire Verge in), 2 Island, Mountain, Swamp.
- Ramp (9 rocks): Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Fellwar Stone, three Signets, three Talismans; plus Don's Treasures, Ramirez, Malcolm, Locke, Gonti.
- Theft (Don's static): Hostage Taker, Gilded Drake, Insurrection, Coercive Recruiter, Thieving Amalgam, Jhoira, Hurl Through Hell, Animate Dead, Reanimate, and now Treachery.
- Foreign casts (Don's Treasures): Etali, Plargg and Nassari, Grenzo, Ramirez, Laughing Jasper Flint, Locke, Stolen Strategy, Wand of Wonder, Siphon Insight, Arcane Heist, You Find Some Prisoners, Thief of Sanity, Gonti, Ragavan, Dauthi Voidwalker, Opposition Agent, Tasha, Black Cat, Praetor's Grasp, Outrageous Robbery, Brainstealer Dragon, Decadent Dragon, Dire Fleet Daredevil, Thieving Varmint, Vaan; Professional Face-Breaker (cut, own cards); and now Gríma and Fallen Shinobi.
- Pirate payoffs: Admiral Beckett Brass, Malcolm, Breeches x2, Kindred Discovery, Roaming Throne, Coercive Recruiter, Vaan, Black Market Connections.
- Interaction: Fierce Guardianship, Mana Drain, Deflecting Swat, Chaos Warp, Cyclonic Rift, Deadly Rollick, Feed the Swarm, Toxic Deluge, Blasphemous Act (cut), Seize the Spotlight (cut), Lightning Greaves.
- Tutors: Vampiric Tutor, Court of Locthwain.
Overlaps: three board wipes that kill our own stolen army; an opponent-choice theft spell; an impulse engine that plays our own cards; two lands usually tapped early.
whole_deck_audit.mana_base_and_curve: Baseline: 35 lands (4 basics), 9 rocks; conditional/early-tapped lands 5; average nonland MV 3.312; 28 creatures; 19 instants/sorceries. Candidate: 35 lands, conditional/early-tapped 3; average nonland MV 3.297; 29 creatures; 17 instants/sorceries. Exact lands-only hypergeometric (mechanics test): Don on turn 4 (4 lands covering U, B, R among 10 cards) 0.4898 -> 0.4864 with each Verge counted at one colour, 0.4898 with the Verge condition met; three lands paying U, B and R among 9 cards 0.5844 -> 0.5740 (0.5844 condition met). Red land sources 22 -> 21 (22 with Blazemire's {R}); P(two / three red lands among 13 cards) 0.8396/0.5901 -> 0.8169/0.5529. Rocks and Treasures excluded (conservative); the tempo of two lands that are untapped on turns 1-2 is not modelled.
whole_deck_audit.interaction_resilience: Stack: Fierce Guardianship, Mana Drain, Deflecting Swat. Removal: Chaos Warp, Deadly Rollick, Feed the Swarm, Hurl Through Hell, Otawara; theft as removal (Treachery new, Hostage Taker, Gilded Drake). Wipes: Toxic Deluge, Cyclonic Rift (Blasphemous Act cut). Protection: Lightning Greaves. Weak points: Don dies to removal and the static disappears immediately (stolen creatures lose menace/deathtouch); graveyard hate stops Animate Dead/Reanimate; creature-light or empty-library-pressure opponents blunt theft; Treasures enter tapped.

material_candidates.source: EDHREC Don general 3121/6802, upgraded 219/480, optimized 28/68; live Scryfall batch
material_candidates.role: {2}{U}{B} 1/4 legendary Human Advisor: can't be blocked; on combat damage to a player, that player exiles cards from the top until an instant or sorcery, and we may cast it free.
material_candidates.incumbent_opportunity_cost: Loses Professional Face-Breaker ({2}{R} menace: a Treasure when our creatures connect, and sacrifice-a-Treasure impulse draw of OUR OWN cards).
material_candidates.commander_synergy: Every cast through Gríma is a real opponent-owned noncreature spell we cast (108.3, 707.10: not a copy), so Don makes two tapped Treasures each hit, and Vaan and Tasha also trigger. Unblockable means it connects even through Don-buffed blockers; it is the deck's most reliable foreign-noncreature engine per turn.
material_candidates.adversarial_downside: Not a Pirate (Roaming Throne naming Pirate doesn't double its trigger; Malcolm/Breeches don't see it); 1 power; a whiff when the opponent's library has few instants/sorceries; dies to any removal. Face-Breaker's Treasure plus impulse is genuine value, but it plays our own cards, which Don never rewards.
material_candidates.reason: Converts combat into opponent-owned spell casts every turn, the second half of Don's Oracle; the cut plays only our own cards.

material_candidates.source: EDHREC Don general 1623/6802, upgraded 126/480, optimized 19/68; live Scryfall batch
material_candidates.role: {3}{U}{B} 3/4 Zombie Ninja, ninjutsu {2}{U}{B}: on combat damage, that player exiles the top two cards; we may play them free this turn.
material_candidates.incumbent_opportunity_cost: Loses Seize the Spotlight ({2}{R} sorcery: each opponent picks fame (we steal a creature until end of turn) or fortune (we draw and make a Treasure); the opponent chooses, so they pick what hurts us least).
material_candidates.commander_synergy: Two opponent-owned cards per hit, free; noncreature ones are Don Treasure triggers (expected 2*(noncreature/85) per hit, 12/17 at 30 noncreature cards; mechanics test) and creature ones enter under our control, so Don makes them +2/+2 menace deathtouch Pirates. Ninjutsu returns the unblocked attacker to its owner's hand (702.49a/c): bouncing a stolen creature hands it back, so we return our own Breeches, Ragavan or Gríma instead.
material_candidates.adversarial_downside: 5 mana hard-cast; ninjutsu needs an unblocked attacker and the right timing; lands exiled can be played only if we have a land drop left.
material_candidates.reason: A card that turns one connected attack into two free foreign cards beats an opponent-choice spell.

material_candidates.source: EDHREC Don general 468/6802, upgraded 40/480, optimized 12/68; live Scryfall batch
material_candidates.role: {3}{U}{U} Aura: enchant creature; when it enters, untap up to five lands; we control enchanted creature.
material_candidates.incumbent_opportunity_cost: Loses Blasphemous Act (cheap symmetric 13-damage wipe), one of three board resets (with Toxic Deluge and Cyclonic Rift).
material_candidates.commander_synergy: Permanent theft of the best opposing creature for effectively 0 mana (five lands untap): the stolen creature is ours to control but not to own, so Don makes it +2/+2 menace deathtouch Pirate (Coercive Recruiter, Malcolm, Admiral Beckett and Breeches see it); the untapped lands then cast the next stolen spell the same turn, which Don's tapped Treasures cannot (111.10a, enter tapped).
material_candidates.adversarial_downside: Aura removal returns the creature (303.4e); Blasphemous Act was the cheapest answer to a wide board. A sweeper also kills our own stolen army and Don, so in this deck it is a reset button, not a plan card. Four-swap list keeping it is staged.
material_candidates.reason: Theft is the deck's plan; a wipe that kills our own Pirates is the worst-fitting interaction slot.

final_changes.coherent_package_tradeoff: Five one-for-one swaps that add opponent-card casting (Gríma, Fallen Shinobi), permanent theft (Treachery) and untapped mana (two Verges). Losses: Professional Face-Breaker's Treasure and impulse draw, Seize the Spotlight's cheap one-turn theft or draw, Blasphemous Act's cheap wipe (Toxic Deluge and Cyclonic Rift remain), Shipwreck Marsh and Smoldering Marsh's fetchability (six fetches now find one fewer typed dual each). Game Changers 5 -> 5.

multi_slot_packages.result_and_rationale: Selected five-swap package, commander-first: two combat engines that cast opponents' cards for free (Gríma for instants/sorceries, Fallen Shinobi for any two), permanent creature theft that buffs under Don (Treachery), and two untapped Verges for two mostly-tapped lands. 35 lands; conditional/early-tapped lands 5 -> 3.
Staged four-swap keeping Blasphemous Act (no Treachery). Retained alternative for an owner who wants a second sweeper.
Staged five-swap with Dazzling Sphinx instead of Gríma. Rejected: 5 mana and blockable.
Staged Pass C Stage A six-swap. Rejected after the bounded grid; owner choice.

low_swap_heightened_audit.alternate_cuts_for_prior_holds: Pass C's Stage A +Mob Rule/-Insurrection and its Bribery vs Thieving Amalgam/Jhoira question were run as bounded finite tests; all three are staged as complete six-swap 100s and rejected (Bribery is also owner-removed). Pass C's final KEEP of Insurrection is respected; the Mob Rule six is the owner's choice if cheaper RR mass theft is preferred.
low_swap_heightened_audit.strongest_argument_against_baseline: Don rewards stealing and casting opponents' cards, yet the baseline carried a wipe that kills the stolen army and Don (Blasphemous Act), a theft spell whose mode the opponents choose (Seize the Spotlight), a value creature that only plays our own cards (Professional Face-Breaker) and two duals that are tapped on turns 1-2.
low_swap_heightened_audit.evidence_based_answer: Five swaps, all commander-first: two combat engines that cast opponents' cards for free (Gríma, Fallen Shinobi), permanent theft that is effectively free (Treachery), and two untapped Verges. Bounded Pass C tests are in the mechanics test. Spellbook: 0 included combos before and after.

final_candidate.deckwide_reconciliation: Commander first, then lines alphabetically; 2x Island, everything else 1x. Five substitutions against the canonical source. 35 lands; 100 physical cards verified by quantity (99 library + 1 commander).

owner_authority.owner_approval_question: This deck is complete. Do you approve it?

open_ended_optimization_audit.remaining_99_review: The five-swap floor was reached with five swaps that each stand on their own; the floor was not used as a target and no sixth swap cleared the bar. Every remaining incumbent was re-read against the candidate pool: twelve post-floor challenges were recorded and rejected on Don-specific grounds, and four six-swap packages (Pass C's Mob Rule over Insurrection; Pass C's Bribery over Thieving Amalgam and over Jhoira; Nightveil Specter over Locke) are staged as complete 100s.

post_floor_challenges.tradeoff: Bounded grid: Mob Rule is castable at 6-7 where Insurrection isn't, but at 8 keeps 115/144 of the stolen power and leaves blockers; RR vs RRR is a real gain (0.84 vs 0.59 lands-only). Pass C KEEP kept; staged.
Bribery's one body (zero at creature density 0) vs 3 manifests per round that Don makes Pirates; owner-removed.
Jhoira's ETB already equals Bribery for historic permanents and repeats on attack; owner-removed.
Specter keeps exiled cards indefinitely but must connect in the air; Locke sees every player's card and makes Treasure on lands.
Owner rejected Memory Plunder; 35 lands + 9 rocks is the minimum ramp for a 3.30 average nonland MV.

Riverpyre (OFF-RANKING, absent from all Don pages) is a third Verge, but Orchard usually makes all three colours in a four-player game while Riverpyre's {U} needs an Island or a Mountain (only 9 such lands).
Vaan counts Pirates, so every Don-buffed stolen creature and every foreign cast grows the board; Robber's hand-size condition fails late.
Crew is owner-rejected; BMC's changeling token is ours (no Don buff) but is a Pirate for Coercive Recruiter and Roaming Throne, and BMC draws and ramps.
Don has no targeted ability, so Greaves' shroud costs nothing and the 0 equip re-protects new thieves.
Deluge is the remaining cheap sweeper with Cyclonic Rift after cutting Blasphemous Act.
Tapped Treasures don't fund the Betrayal turn; Siphon flashes back and banks a card.
Zara is owner-removed; Plargg casts two free opposing spells each upkeep.

larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: Bounded grid: at 8 mana Insurrection steals at least as much on 5/5 tables and leaves no blockers; Pass C's final KEEP and the approved list keep it.

larger_swap_packages.case_for_extra_swaps: Pass C named it: Bribery picks the best creature immediately and costs one mana less than Jhoira.
larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: Owner-removed on 2026-10-14; Jhoira matches Bribery on entering and repeats on every attack that survives.

larger_swap_packages.case_for_extra_swaps: Long-lived access to exiled opposing cards for as long as Nightveil Specter lives, at three mana.
larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: Marginal; Locke sees every player's milled card each attack and makes a Treasure on lands, and is evasive against bigger creatures.

open_ended_optimization_audit.quality_based_stop_reason: Stopped at five. Each remaining weak-looking slot beats its best challenger on Don-specific grounds: Insurrection takes every blocker (bounded grid), Thieving Amalgam and Jhoira out-produce Bribery after one round, Locke and Vaan feed foreign casts and Pirate counters, Fellwar/Exotic Orchard fix a 35-land three-colour list, Lightning Greaves' shroud costs nothing with Don, Toxic Deluge is the remaining cheap wipe, and the owner's 2026-10-14 removals (Bribery, Zara, Memory Plunder, Agent of Treachery, Captivating Crew and others) were not re-added.
